description: A resolved crosswalk linking SEC EDGAR registrants (CIK / ticker / fund series) to their GLEIF Legal Entity Identifier (LEI) — one row per asserted identity, each carrying its provenance tier, method and confidence. Authoritative edges come from official SEC/GLEIF registration (no guessing); the operating-company tail is linked by probabilistic name resolution (Fellegi-Sunter / Splink): exact normalized-name matches are confirmed (~95% precision), while name-only fuzzy matches are surfaced as candidates rather than auto-confirmed. A point-in-time snapshot, with an as-of date on every row.
name: edgar_gleif

fields.description: Scheme of the SEC identifier held in `key`, and the discriminator that says how to read that column. This snapshot carries two: cik (an EDGAR Central Index Key, rendered as decimal digits) and series (an SEC fund identifier, a letter prefix followed by digits). A third scheme, class (fund share class), is producible by the pipeline but is absent from this snapshot.
fields.name: key_type

fields.description: The SEC-side identifier this edge is keyed on, read according to `key_type`: for cik rows an EDGAR Central Index Key in decimal digits with no leading zeros; for series rows an SEC fund identifier — an uppercase letter prefix followed by digits (S…, C…, CEF…). Text, not a number: the two schemes share one column, so the pattern above is their union and no arithmetic type describes it. To join it to `edgar.cik`, render that integer column as text — see `x-joins`.
fields.name: key

fields.description: GLEIF Legal Entity Identifier (ISO 17442): a four-character alphanumeric LOU prefix, fourteen alphanumeric entity characters, then two check digits.
fields.name: lei

fields.description: GLEIF's authoritative entity category (e.g. GENERAL, FUND, BRANCH); GENERAL when unknown.
fields.name: category

fields.description: Jurisdiction the entity is constituted under, as GLEIF records it: an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, or an ISO 3166-2 subdivision code (country, hyphen, subdivision) where GLEIF holds one — US-DE, AE-SH.
fields.name: jurisdiction

fields.description: How the edge was established. Authoritative: sec-registration (GLEIF RA000665) or sec-ncen (SEC Form N-CEN). Probabilistic: exact_name (identical normalized company name) or jaro_winkler (fuzzy name).
fields.name: method

fields.description: Provenance tier, in precedence order: authoritative (deterministic SEC/GLEIF registration — no guessing), confirmed (exact normalized-name Splink match, ~95% precision), candidate (name-only fuzzy match, surfaced NOT asserted), ambiguous (one exact name matched more than one entity). A deterministic edge always wins over a name match for the same key.
fields.name: tier

fields.description: Edge confidence in [0, 1]: 1.0 for authoritative edges; the Fellegi-Sunter posterior match probability under the frozen resolution model for probabilistic edges.
fields.name: confidence

fields.description: Lowercased, accent-stripped concatenation of the display name, legal name, ticker and LEI — a derived free-text search field, not a source attribute.
fields.name: corpus

title: EDGAR ↔ GLEIF — company-to-LEI crosswalk

x-joins.$comment: How to join this crosswalk to the packages it references, and how far each join reaches. These are NOT `schema.foreignKeys`: a Data Package foreign key asserts that every value on the left exists on the right, and neither of these joins satisfies that against the published bytes — see each `cardinality` and `coverage`. Declaring them as foreign keys would advertise a guarantee the data does not keep, so the guarantee is dropped and the reachable part is stated instead. `coverage` is measured against the exact objects this descriptor names in `resources[].path`, and moves when they are republished, exactly as `bytes` and `hash` do.

joins.cardinality: partial — most left rows have no match, and the referenced side also holds keys this crosswalk does not carry. Neither side contains the other.
joins.description: SEC-side identity: a cik-typed edge to the EDGAR company-ticker table. `edgar` is a ticker/exchange listing, not the CIK universe, so it covers a small part of the registrants this crosswalk keys on; the direction of containment runs neither way. Join by rendering `edgar.cik` (an integer) as text and comparing it to `key` (text) — the rendering is exact, because no published CIK carries a leading zero.
joins.evidence: For key_type='cik' rows, `key` is the EDGAR Central Index Key as reported to SEC EDGAR. Where both sides hold the same registrant the values agree exactly; the shortfall is coverage, not disagreement — `edgar` lists only registrants with a ticker on a US venue.
joins.name: edgar

joins.cardinality: partial — nearly every left row matches, but not all. The two packages are point-in-time snapshots taken at different times, so a handful of LEIs on this side are not in the GLEIF file this descriptor names.
joins.description: GLEIF-side identity: every edge carries the LEI it resolved to. Join `lei` to `gleif.lei` directly — both sides are text and no rendering is involved.

evidence.comparison: normalized company name (exact, then Jaro-Winkler tiers)
evidence.method: Fellegi-Sunter probabilistic record linkage (Splink), frozen model, for the operating-company tail; official SEC/GLEIF registration for authoritative edges
evidence.precision: exact normalized-name matches auto-confirmed (~95% precision, spot-checked); name-only fuzzy matches surfaced as candidate, not confirmed
evidence.tie_break: ISSUED > LAPSED > RETIRED, then US jurisdiction

joins.name: gleif

x-joins.verifiedBy: datasets/edgar_gleif/scripts/crosswalk_join.py — runs each join above against the published objects and fails if a declared `coverage` is wrong.
